analysis:
The documentation change in docs/architecture/inference.md is confined to two head ranges: the date update at head line 3 and the new paragraph at head lines 253-259. The new paragraph says the SSD stage runs before engine.submit and off the engine queue. During this stage the engine may hold MLX-Swift's process-wide evalLock for another request's prefill. Provider-staged complete-checkpoint imports create their destinations directly from host bytes and never evaluate or fence them, so staging does not wait for that chunk (CompleteCheckpointTransfer.swift; reference/ssd-kv-cache.md#complete-checkpoint-payload).

The change is documentation only. It does not alter the threat-model-relevant controls under T-041/SEC-035: HMAC lookup names, DBK3 AAD, the 30-min TTL, cacheSalt scoping and staging reservations. Base units 4 and 5 (lines 829-1195) are unchanged context.

One implementation question is outside the supplied evidence. The claim that staged destinations are created from host bytes without evaluation implies that authenticated (AES-GCM verified) payload bytes are materialized directly into MLX arrays. Concurrency between staging and engine evaluation should not race on shared buffers or bypass the GlobalKVCacheBudget staging reservation (SSDPrefixCache.endAdoption/completeStaging). This needs verification against CompleteCheckpointTransfer.swift in the PR's source changes, if present. No regression is evidenced from the documentation alone.
